ROLE: Destroy the session held in registry slot index and shift the following slots down so the registry stays compact and every remaining owned session pointer is still reachable exactly once.

SIGNATURE.RAW: static void remove_session_at(struct broker *b, size_t index)
SIGNATURE.NAME: remove_session_at

STRUCT.NAME: struct broker
STRUCT.ROLE: registry whose slot index is removed and whose tail is shifted down

STRUCT.NAME: struct session
STRUCT.ROLE: owned session destroyed by this function

FUNC.NAME: session_destroy
FUNC.ROLE: close the descriptor if open and free every session-owned resource, including any NULL slot

FUNC.NAME: memmove
FUNC.ROLE: shift the higher slots one position down (regions overlap, so memmove is required)

VAR.NAME: struct broker
VAR.ROLE: b->count is decremented; b->sessions[index] is NULLed before the shift so a partially completed removal could never free the same session twice

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: session_destroy
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: void; the descriptor is closed exactly once if it is still open, the receive buffer, queued output, identifier copy and every filter copy are released, and the object is freed; NULL is ignored
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: transfers ownership of the session to this call: the caller must not use the pointer afterwards, and no other registry slot may hold it
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions; safe on a session that already closed its own descriptor or on a NULL slot

LOGIC.INPUT: b: broker registry whose sessions array and count are valid. index: slot to remove; the caller guarantees index < b->count.
LOGIC.ACTION: 1. s = b->sessions[index]. 2. b->sessions[index] = NULL so the slot cannot be mistaken for a live session even if the shift below is observed reentrantly. 3. session_destroy(s): it releases the descriptor (if still open), the receive and output buffers, the identifier copy and every subscription filter copy, then frees the session object. 4. b->count--. 5. memmove(&b->sessions[index], &b->sessions[index + 1], (b->count - index) * sizeof *b->sessions) moves every later slot down one position; when index == b->count (the removed session was last) the count is already decremented so zero bytes are moved, and b->sessions[old count - 1] is left holding the NULL written in step 2 rather than a duplicate pointer. The array capacity is not changed: the freed slot's storage is retained for the next broker_accept.
LOGIC.OUTPUT: void. The destroyed session's resources are fully released, b->count is one smaller, the slots after index hold the sessions that were previously one position higher, and the trailing slot contains NULL.
INVARIANTS_USED: the broker owns every session pointer in the array; removing one releases exactly its resources
the slots after index overlap the destination, so the shift must use memmove semantics
removing one session never changes another session's descriptor, queue or subscriptions
capacity is retained so a reconnecting client does not force a fresh array allocation
LOGIC.PRECONDITION: b is non-NULL and b->sessions is a valid array with b->count >= 1 and index < b->count; no caller holds a borrowed pointer to the removed session afterwards.
LOGIC.POSTCONDITION: b->count decreased by one, the removed session is destroyed and no registry slot references it, and the relative order of all other sessions is preserved.
LOGIC.THREAD_SAFETY: Single-threaded reactor; the array is not iterated by any other frame while this runs.

EXPECT.note: c moved from slot 2 into slot 1; a untouched
